I read the test class and the `Conditions.evolve` implementation. The key code facts are:

- `evolve` returns immediately at line 105 when `status` is empty, so no local `conditions` dict is ever bound in that branch.
- It also returns immediately at line 117 when every provided status matches the existing condition statuses, again before `conditions` is created.
- Otherwise, line 119 initializes a fresh local `conditions = {}`.
- Then line 121 iterates through `self.conditions.items()`, and line 124 assigns exactly one entry per successful iteration: `conditions[condition] = value.evolve(status=s)`.
- So within any single non-early-return frame, `len(conditions)` starts at 0 and grows by 1 each time line 124 runs, until either the loop finishes or an exception interrupts it.
- Across the whole suite, different calls use different `Conditions` instances with different numbers of conditions (3, 2, 6, compound 3, static 3), and each new non-early-return frame resets `conditions` back to an empty dict at line 119 before growing again.
- Therefore, when concatenating all observations chronologically across all frames, the sequence necessarily contains increases within frames and drops back to 0/1 at the start of later frames, so it cannot be globally non-decreasing or non-increasing.
